note: Adapted from the original English description in Hill 1915. The original describes it as Copritermes taylori, sp. nov. (the heading is OCR'd as "COPRITERMES TaYLORI"); no alate was seen. Type locality Koolpinyah, near Darwin, Northern Territory (G. F. Hill, 21 November 1913, month 11), type number No.89, deposited in the Entomological Branch, Department of Agriculture, Northern Territory. The original records one nest containing a gravid neoteinic queen, a king, 2 neoteinic queens, about 15 soldiers, about 100 workers, many nymphs and eggs; the nest was a mass about 3 inches in diameter made of chewed wood and earth, beneath the soil surface at the base of a fence-post support. The species is named after Frank H. Taylor, entomologist at the Australian Institute of Tropical Medicine, Queensland.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head pale yellow, with white rings at the base and tip of each antennal segment; mandibles dark chestnut brown; the rest dull white. Length 2½ mm (excluding the mandibles), mandibles 1 mm. Head long, slender, cylindrical, rounded behind, the sides straight as far as the antennal fossae, truncate in front, the frons produced forwards into a long conical process, slightly upturned, extending forwards to the tip of the labrum. Clypeus small, anterior margin rounded, white. Labrum long, slightly narrowed towards the tip, the tip produced on each side into a point bearing a few long hairs. Antennae long, slender, hairy, 14-segmented, arising from round fossae in angular depressions at the sides of the head; 1st segment long, stout, nearly cylindrical; 2nd half as long as the 1st, slender; 3rd and 4th small, moniliform; 5th—13th becoming longer and slightly turbinate; 14th longer than the 13th, elongate-oval. Mandibles extremely long, longer than the head, curved, slender, arising from the middle of the head, curving downwards almost to the tip, the tip rather straight and flattened on one side; the base of the left mandible bears a large blunt tusk, opposed by a blunt process on the right. Pronotum small, not wider than the head, the anterior half rounded in front and turned up almost at a right angle, the sides sloping to the posterior margin, the posterior margin slightly concave in the middle. Abdomen elongate-oval, circular in cross-section. Femora flattened; tibiae long and slender, the apical spur small, the claws large. Cerci small, hairy.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head and antennae paler than in the soldier, the clypeus with rust-coloured spots at the ends. Head large, round, more hairy than in the soldier. Clypeus large, convex, rounded and lobed at the posterior margin. Labrum large, rounded at the anterior margin. Antennae 14-segmented, hairy, the 3rd and 4th segments smallest. Legs stout; tibial spurs small; claws large. Cerci small, hairy. The posterior opening appears to be often swollen, as in the soldier. Length 3 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Neoteinic queen (neoteinic in the original): the sclerites of the head, thorax and abdomen pale yellow, the legs and antennae paler, the rest milky white. Length 5 mm. Posterior part of the head rounded; frons concave; compound eyes round, projecting from the sides of the head, with fine facets; ocelli round, in line with the anterior margin of the compound eyes; clypeus large, convex, the posterior margin arched, divided by a longitudinal suture that extends across the concave frons, the anterior margin rounded and depressed, separated from the posterior part by deep lateral sutures. Labrum large, projecting beyond the mandibles, widest at the posterior part, narrowing to a blunt apex. Antennae hairy, 15-segmented, short and slender, arising from round fossae in front of the compound eyes; 1st segment long, slightly turbinate; 2nd half as long as the 1st, cylindrical; 3rd minute; 4th—10th larger, fused; 11th, 12th and 13th progressively larger; 14th long, nearly cylindrical; 15th elongate-oval, slightly stalked, longer than the 14th. Pronotum long, narrower than the head, saddle-shaped, the anterior margin truncate and rigid, the sides and posterior margin rounded; wing buds vestigial. Tarsi slender, claws small. Cerci small, conical. Head, thorax, abdomen and legs entirely covered with fine pale hairs. King (Male, king in the original): dorsum dark brown, head chestnut brown, antennae dark brown with whitish base and tip of each segment, legs and ventral sclerites pale brown. Length 3½ mm. Posterior part of the head rounded, the vertex flat, sloping down to the projecting clypeus, with a curious keyhole-shaped white spot in the middle of the depression between the eyes. Compound eyes large, projecting, clearly extending beyond the sides of the mouth; ocelli large, kidney-shaped, close to the inner margin of the compound eyes. Antennae hairy, 15-segmented; 1st segment long, stout, cylindrical; 2nd half as long; 3rd minute; 4th—10th moniliform; 11th—14th becoming longer; 15th largest, elongate-oval. Clypeus paler than the head, large, convex, the posterior margin arched, the tip white, separated from the basal two-thirds by a deep transverse suture. Labrum large, covering the mandibles, narrow at the base, bulging at the sides in the middle, then narrowing to a rounded tip. Pronotum long, wrinkled, narrower than the head, the anterior margin truncate and slightly curved forwards. Femora stout and flattened; tibiae slender; apical spurs and claws large. Egg: pale yellow, curved, bluntly rounded at both ends, length ½ mm.
